Here's what economists sayPublished Sat, Sep 28 202410:00 AM EDTGreg Iacurci@GregIacurciWATCH LIVEKey PointsImmigration is a top issue in the 2024 U.S. presidential election for supporters of former President Donald Trump, the Republican nominee.Trump has said at campaign events that immigrants are taking jobs away from U.S.-born workers.Labor economists say immigrants benefit the overall job market and economy. There's an ongoing debate about impact on wages for workers without high school degrees.The first debate between Vice President Kamala Harris and former President Donald Trump is shown on television at the Juventud 2000 migrant shelter in Tijuana, Mexico, on Sept. 10, 2024. Immigration has been a hot topic throughout the presidential campaign.Carlos Moreno/NurPhoto via Getty ImagesThe idea that immigration has a negative impact on the U.S. job market is a common theme of former President Donald Trump's speeches on the presidential campaign trail."They're taking your jobs," the Republican nominee told supporters on Sept. 21 in Wilmington, North Carolina.Immigration is also a top issue for Republican voters: 82% of Trump supporters say immigration is "very important" to their vote in the 2024 presidential election, second only to the economy, according to the Pew Research Center. It's the lowest-priority issue for Democrats, Pew found. Pew polled 9,720 U.S. adults from Aug. 26 through Sept. 2.However, evidence suggests immigrants help the overall economy. And, at a high level, they aren't taking jobs from or reducing the wages of U.S.-born (or so-called native) workers, according to economists who study the impact of immigration on the labor market."Overall, the consensus is very strong that there are not significant costs to U.S.-born workers from immigration, at least the type of immigration we have historically had in the U.S.," said Alexander Arnon, director of business tax and economic analysis at the Penn Wharton Budget Model.Immigrants expected to boost the economyThere are several reasons why immigrants largely benefit the economy and job market, economists said.For one, the job market isn't static.Immigrants take jobs but they also create new ones by spending in local economies and by starting businesses, economists said. One 2020 research paper from the National Bureau of Economic Research found immigrants are 80% more likely to become entrepreneurs than native workers.A recent "surge" of immigrants to the U.S. is expected to add $8.9 trillion (or 3.2%) to the nation's GDP over the next decade, according to the Congressional Budget Office, a nonpartisan scorekeeper for Congress.watch nowVIDEO7:1807:18The 2024 election is going to come down to immigration and affordability, says pollster Frank LuntzSquawk Box"That's enormous," said Michael Clemens, a professor at George Mason University and an economist whose research examines the economic causes and effects of migration. "That creates jobs, that raises pay, that is an increase in the size and complexity of the U.S. economy."Immigrants also aren't perfect substitutes for U.S. citizens in many job positions; in fact, the two groups often complement each other rather than compete, economists said.However, some economic research suggests immigration can impact the wages of certain subgroups of U.S.-born workers, especially those with lower levels of educational attainment.Overall, the consensus is very strong that there are not significant costs to U.S.-born workers from immigration.Alexander Arnondirector of business tax and economic analysis at the Penn Wharton Budget ModelSome economists contend an influx of immigrants can reduce wages for such Americans in the short term, though other researchers have found that Americans ultimately benefit, partly because those in direct competition with immigrants are able to find higher-paying jobs."Not everybody agrees about it," Clemens said.A big supply of new labor due to immigration can be "difficult and anxiety-inducing" for American workers who must adjust, he added."But people end up in better circumstances," he said.Immigration helped cool 'overheated' job marketThe El Chaparral pedestrian border crossing at the San Ysidro Port of Entry in Tijuana, Mexico, on Jan. 4, 2024. Carlos Moreno/Bloomberg via Getty ImagesImmigrants accounted for about 14% of the U.S. population in 2022, according to Pew, citing most recently available federal data.Most are in the U.S. legally: Undocumented immigrants represented 3.3% of the total U.S. population and 23% of immigrants in 2022, Pew said. Their number has increased in recent years, to 11 million, but remains below its 2007 peak of more than 12 million.The number of immigrants coming to the U.S. has "increased sharply in recent years," the CBO wrote in July.More from Personal Finance:How the presidential election could affect your taxesJudge blocks Biden's new student loan forgiveness planHarris wants to raise the top capital gains tax rate to 28%Net immigration is expected to be 8.7 million people higher from 2021 to 2026 than would have been extrapolated from pre-Covid migration trends, the CBO said. (Its analysis excludes those with green cards.)The influx has been beneficial for the pandemic-era economy, economists said.It "helped cool an overheated labor market" over the past two years, Elior Cohen, an economist at the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, wrote in May.Demand for workers hit historic highs as the U.S. economy started to reopen in 2021. Wages rose sharply — at their fastest pace in decades — as businesses competed for workers, putting upward pressure on high inflation.Immigrant labor alleviated "severe staffing shortages," especially in industries like leisure and hospitality, helping dilute those inflationary wage pressures, Cohen wrote.In this sense, immigrants weren't competing with U.S. citizens for jobs but instead taking a surplus of available jobs, said Giovanni Peri, an economics professor and director of the Global Migration Center at the University of California, Davis.In fact, a long-term net decline in the number of non-college-educated immigrants to the U.S. from 2010 to 2021 likely contributed to those recent labor shortages, he said."If there is a time when low-skilled immigration isn't competing with natives and helping fill shortages, it's been the last two years," Peri said.'Little evidence' of employment impactEven before the Covid-19 pandemic, economists from varying sides of the debate published a "consensus" viewpoint in 2017 on the job market effect of immigration, Clemens said.The panel of economists found "little evidence that immigration significantly affects" overall employment levels among Americans, they wrote for the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine."I'd say the consensus has gotten [even] stronger" since then, said Arnon of the Penn Wharton Budget Model, who authored a separate 2016 analysis of existing research on immigration's economic impact.To the extent there's job competition from new immigrants, it tends to fall mostly on prior immigrants rather than native U.S. workers, according to the National Academies paper.Prior immigrants are most likely to experience "negative wage effects," it said.However, native-born high school dropouts may experience that effect, as well, since they "share job qualifications similar to the large share of low-skilled [immigrant] workers," the National Academies paper said.Immigrants without a high school degree account for the largest share of foreign-born workers, followed by those with graduate or professional degrees, according to the Penn Wharton analysis.A heated debate on low-skilled workersA boat arrives in Key West, Florida with Cuban refugees in April 1980 from Mariel Harbor after crossing the Florida Straits.Tim Chapman | Miami Herald | Getty ImagesOne influential — and controversial — paper by Harvard economist George Borjas echoes that finding about high school dropouts.Borjas — who was among the more than three dozen economists who authored the National Academies consensus paper — studied the Mariel boatlift, a mass emigration of 125,000 Cuban refugees to South Florida from April to October 1980.At least 60% of these "Marielitos" were high school dropouts, he said. Borjas found that the large boost in labor supply caused the wages of high school dropouts in Miami to drop "dramatically," by 10% to 30%.Stephen Miller, a senior policy adviser during the Trump administration, cited the paper in 2017 as a justification for a new proposal to curtail legal immigration, particularly among lower-skilled workers.Asked to comment on Trump's campaign statements about immigration and jobs, Anna Kelly, a spokeswoman for the Republican National Committee, said in an emailed statement that the former president "has never wavered in his promise to put America First, including workers born in the USA and incentivizing companies to keep jobs at home."watch nowVIDEO2:2402:24US election to come "right down to the wire": Evercore ISISquawk Box AsiaBorjas' finding was in contrast with earlier work by economist and Nobel laureate David Card, who had found the Mariel boatlift didn't increase unemployment or negatively affect wages of "less-skilled" non-Cuban or Cuban workers.Some economists, including Clemens, dispute Borjas' findings. Borjas didn't return a request for comment."Sudden surges of immigration obviously affect the ability of native workers to find and take jobs on a given afternoon," Clemens said.But immigrants "also create jobs," Clemens said. "A large preponderance of evidence is the job creation effect overwhelms the competition effect, even in the short term."Effect may depend on the economic environmentMigrant workers pick strawberries during harvest south of San Francisco.Joe Sohm/Visions Of America | Universal Images Group | Getty ImagesNative U.S. workers and immigrants, even those with similar educational backgrounds, tend to complement each other via their skills, making each other more productive and in essence jointly creating each other's jobs, Clemens said.For example, in a restaurant, a native worker with better command of spoken English might be a waiter, while an immigrant might do kitchen-prep work or wash dishes, tasks that don't require such language dexterity. On farms, native workers might be supervisors or run high-tech equipment while immigrants handpick crops, Clemens said.Research by Peri and Alessandro Caiumi of the University of California, Davis, finds that factors like "occupational upgrading" generally lead native workers who initially compete with immigrants for jobs to earn higher wages in the future.For example, from 2000 to 2019, such factors helped boost wages for less-educated native workers by a "significant" 1.7% to 2.6%, and there was also "no significant wage effect on college educated natives," Peri and Caiumi wrote. Similarly, from 2019 to 2022, estimates suggest "small positive effects" on wages.Ultimately, "what might have happened in Florida during the Mariel boatlift in the 1980s may be different than what happens in Arizona in the 2010s," said Michael Strain, director of economic policy studies at the American Enterprise Institute, a right-leaning think tank."From a policy perspective, you have to figure out which of the studies are most relevant to the current economic environment you're considering," Strain said.Subscribe to CNBC PROSubscribe to Investing ClubLicensing & ReprintsCNBC CouncilsSelect Personal FinanceCNBC on PeacockJoin the CNBC PanelSupply Chain ValuesSelect ShoppingClosed CaptioningDigital ProductsNews ReleasesInternshipsCorrectionsAbout CNBCAd ChoicesSite MapPodcastsCareersHelpContactNews TipsGot a confidential news tip? TrendsGetting the Most Out of 1F by Allegro: Success Stories

By Editorial Teamaccess_time3 hours ago



 

Logistics plays a huge role when scaling your eCommerce business globally. Managing inventory, shipping, and customer satisfaction across borders can pose a lot of challenges, especially when trying to maintain efficiency and speed. That’s where One Fulfillment by Allegro steps in. Today, we’ll not only explore what this solution offers and its many benefits, but more importantly, we’ll show you three real-life success stories that showcase just how impactful it can be for your business.
What is One Fulfillment by Allegro?
One Fulfillment by Allegro is a comprehensive logistics solution that allows eCommerce businesses to outsource their storage, packing, and shipping operations. It is designed to streamline the order fulfillment process, reducing lead times and enhancing customer satisfaction. 

With Allegro handling the logistics, sellers can focus more on growing their business. Success metrics highlight its effectiveness: offers on fulfillment accounts see a 534% surge in page views compared to those on regular accounts, and 80% of offers achieve Purchase Value (PV) in the first month.
How does One Fulfillment by Allegro work?
The process of using One Fulfillment by Allegro is straightforward and efficient:

Create a Seller account: First, you need to set up a new One Fulfillment seller account on Allegro. This gives you access to the platform’s fulfillment services.
Prepare your offers: Select the products you wish to sell using One Fulfillment. These items will be shipped from Allegro’s warehouses, so it’s important to plan ahead.
Send products to Allegro Warehouse: You ship your inventory directly to Allegro’s warehouse, where their team takes over the logistics process. They handle inventory management, order picking, and packing.
Shipping: Orders are dispatched on the same day of purchase or within 24 hours, providing fast and reliable delivery to customers. Allegro also manages customer inquiries, returns, and provides multi-country delivery options (Poland, Czechia, Slovakia).

Benefits of One Fulfillment by Allegro
One Fulfillment by Allegro offers several key benefits that make it an indispensable solution for businesses aiming to scale efficiently:

Cut logistics costs: Through outsourcing logistics to Allegro, you reduce warehousing, shipping, and operational costs. In turn, businesses are able to reallocate funds to marketing and product development, which fuels growth.
Expand without storage limitations: Allegro provides the storage space you need, eliminating the constraints of physical inventory storage. You can expand your product line without worrying about additional warehousing expenses.
Seamless international expansion: One Fulfillment supports businesses expanding into Poland, but also Czechia and Slovakia, providing fast cross-border shipping without the hassle of managing international logistics contracts. Tap into new markets with ease!
Same-day delivery: Impress your customers with same-day or next-day delivery. A speedy delivery time enhances customer satisfaction, making repeat purchases more likely.
Eco-friendly packaging: Allegro is committed to sustainability, using recycled materials for packaging. Besides reducing environmental impact, this also appeals to eco-conscious consumers.
24/7 support and hassle-free returns: Allegro’s professional customer service team handles order-related inquiries from 7:00 am to midnight CET and manages returns for you. 
Improve sales with better visibility: Products on One Fulfillment accounts benefit from higher visibility, with special badges like the Super Seller badge raising trust and attracting more customers. On top of that, participation in promotions and campaigns such as Smart Week and Black Friday can further increase sales.

1F by Allegro: success stories
No matter how well we describe the benefits of One Fulfillment, nothing speaks louder than the success stories of real businesses that have transformed their operations. 
Hearing about tangible results from companies shows exactly how Allegro’s fulfillment services can take eCommerce to new heights – so, without further ado, let’s present them!
#1 FOREO



Learn more: https://allegro.pl/akademia/tip/success-story-foreo-europe-mini 
FOREO, a global beauty tech company, entered the industry with a mission to bring spa-quality wellness treatments into the home. Their product range includes popular devices like the Luna facial cleansing brush, the Bare microcurrent facial toning device, and their latest anti-aging brand, FAQ. Despite their success in many markets, they faced challenges when expanding into Poland.
Initially, FOREO shipped products from Croatia to Poland, resulting in delivery times of up to five business days, which did not meet the high expectations of Polish consumers. Petra Vranješ, e-Key Account Specialist at FOREO, explains, “We switched to One Fulfillment in mid-2022, which meant for the Polish customers that they can get their package much faster.” This switch significantly improved delivery speed and allowed customers to choose from multiple delivery options.
The benefits didn’t stop there. Through joining Allegro’s One Fulfillment service, FOREO earned the coveted Smart! badge, which guarantees free delivery and returns for customers. By earning this badge, FOREO not only gained customer trust, but was also able to take part in key promotional events. Vranješ highlights the importance of this strategy: “Participate in all the campaigns you can, and of course, if you have the possibility, switch to One Fulfillment, definitely.”
FOREO actively takes part in major Allegro campaigns, such as Black Week and Christmas, driving visibility and sales. During Black Week 2023, for example, they sold over 800 products, illustrating the power of Allegro’s promotional opportunities. The company also emphasizes the importance of optimizing product listings on Allegro, making them clear and high-quality to attract customers and maintain sales momentum.
With the help of One Fulfillment and Allegro’s promotional tools, FOREO has not only solidified its presence in Poland but also expanded into Czechia and Slovakia. Vranješ notes, “We truly appreciate our customers and the trust we get from Allegro platform”.
#2 Trust



Learn more: https://allegro.pl/akademia/tip/success-story-trust-international-bv-mini
Trust is a leading player in the consumer electronics industry, specializing in gaming accessories, mobile accessories, and computer peripherals. Their focus is on providing high-quality electronics for home office environments, and when the company decided to expand into Poland, Allegro stood out as their first choice for entering the marketplace.
With Allegro being their first marketplace experience, Marialena Panagiotidou, Marketplaces Specialist at Trust, explains the logic behind their decision: “We started it in the Poland market and that’s because we thought it’s the right way to go because of its prominence in the Polish market.” Trust saw immense potential in Allegro’s reach, particularly due to the platform’s visibility and established customer base.
Given the low average order value of their products, Trust quickly realized that delivering from their base in the Netherlands would be both costly and inefficient. They opted for One Fulfillment by Allegro early on to ensure faster delivery times, reduce logistics overhead, and ease the burden on their customer service team. “We did go with One Fulfillment right away for fastest delivery, less effort from our side, from customer service, logistics, etcetera,” says Panagiotidou.
In addition to speeding up logistics, One Fulfillment played a pivotal role in helping Trust earn the Super Seller Badge. This badge boosted their visibility on the platform, enabling Trust to participate in key Allegro campaigns like Smart Week, Black Friday, and Christmas promotions. For instance, their participation in Smart Week in May saw a surge in monthly revenue. Trust also found that sponsored offers were the most effective paid advertising option, driving strong conversion rates.
Want to go a different route? That’s possible as well
Bonus success story: Electronic Star
“Allegro became the one and only alternative for us, and it became evident that we must be on the Allegro,” says Jana Lacková, Head of Marketplace CEE at Electronic Star.



Learn more: https://allegro.pl/akademia/tip/success-story-electronic-star-mini 
Electronic Star is a multi-category retailer with a broad range of over 250 product categories, including electronics, home appliances, and garden items. 
The company successfully entered the Polish market, and although they recognized the benefits of optimizing logistics, they have chosen to operate without Allegro’s One Fulfillment for now. Still, being on Allegro allowed them to reach thousands of new customers in Poland. Jana Lacková mentioned several opportunities worth exploring, such as the Allegro Smart! badge, which helped them gain better visibility. She also said that she would encourage every international seller to start selling on Allegro, emphasizing the benefits that Electronic Star has experienced firsthand.
However, switching to One Fulfillment by Allegro is on their agenda for the future. Lacková explains that adapting to Allegro’s fulfillment model is a key challenge for them, but they see tremendous potential in doing so. “We would like to, of course, try One Fulfillment of Allegro. It’s one of the challenges for us to change the processes within our company and to adapt them to Allegro models,” she says, noting that faster deliveries and improved customer service could help boost their sales and revenue significantly.
Electronic Star also has ambitions beyond Poland, with plans to expand into Czechia, Slovakia, and other Allegro markets as they open. They have the products and infrastructure ready in these regions, so this expansion is high on their priority list.
Ready to Switch to One Fulfillment by Allegro Yet?
If handling logistics feels like juggling too many balls at once, One Fulfillment by Allegro might just be the answer you’ve been looking for. With faster delivery, less hassle, and badges that boost your visibility, it’s ideal for businesses ready to level up in Poland and beyond. 
Brands like FOREO, Electronic Star, and Trust have already experienced smoother operations and increasing sales thanks to this service. 
Why not let Allegro handle the logistics while you focus on growing your brand? Ready to make the switch? See how One Fulfillment by Allegro can take your eCommerce to the next level!
